status_at_declaration: prospective; not executed; frozen by build_package.py which adds source pins and SHA-256

questions.E1_H2: At identical PCG work on physical topology-optimization states, is the FP64 modal8 solve faster than the fastest published FP64 fused baseline on an RTX 4090?
questions.time_to_tolerance: Which of FP64 PCG and the donor's mixed-precision refinement reaches the 1e-8 true residual fastest, with and without modal8?
questions.E3_H4: In FP32 on the same GPU, does modal8 still beat the fastest FP32 baseline? (Roofline predicts no.)

fixed_iterations_source: JPDC profile v2: converged fused_ai_fp64 iteration counts per case (evidence/solve-profile-rtx4090/local-verification.json). Fixed-work solves run pcg with tol=0 and maxiter=fixed_iterations, so every path performs identical iterations and matvec calls.

fixed_work.design: paired rounds; each round runs every FP64 path once in a fresh random order

products.vector: seeded standard normal, constrained DOFs zeroed

h2.rule: continue modal8 iff both primary cases pass with identical work and all rounds present; otherwise stop modal8

h4.rule: prediction confirmed iff modal8_fp32 median paired ratio vs the fastest FP32 baseline < 1.10 on both primary cases; either outcome is reported

decision.time_to_tolerance: descriptive; the paper's end-to-end claim is stated against the fastest method that physically passes at the same tolerance

exclusions: Process/context import, reference compilation, independent CPU replay and archive I/O are outside solve timers and recorded separately. Setup (construction, compilation, material, diagonal, one capped iteration) is timed per path and reported, not hidden.
